subject: hydra
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: five-headed hydra.
Style: God of War.

spec.name: Hydra of the Broken Axes
spec.description: A scarred, battle-worn five-headed Norse hydra in a gritty God of War style: slate-green scales, bone horns, rusted iron bands and embedded broken weapons, with ember-orange eyes and frost-blue runes glowing against the muted pelt.
spec.layout: A huge four-legged reptilian brute standing on a bare floor. It faces +Z. The body is a heavy barrel with a high shoulder hump, from z -2.0 to 2.3 and about y 1.2 to 3.3. Four thick pillar legs stand at x = ±1.1..1.55: short stocky forelegs at the front and digitigrade hindlegs behind. A long low tail runs back to z = -5.1, tapering to a bone spade tip. Five necks rise from the shoulder hump (z ~1.5, y ~2.8) in a fan, each an S-curve ending in a head that looks forward (+Z). From the centre outward the head heights are: centre (x 0, head y ~5.0, tallest, alpha, biggest, scale 1.25), inner pair (x ±2.0, head y ~4.5, scale 1.0), outer pair (x ±2.95, head y ~3.55, lowest, angled outward, scale 0.85). Rest pose: necks spread apart and extended, every jaw built as a separate upper and lower jaw so it can open, tails and legs extended and neutral. Style (God of War): heavy, brutal, weathered, grounded. Chunky blocky silhouettes and faceted low-poly forms. Desaturated cold slate-green hide with paler weathered ash-bone belly and throat plates. Every part is scarred: long pale scar-tissue gashes, cauterised burn patches, broken horn tips wrapped in iron bands, chipped teeth. Worn rusty iron and bronze bands, chains and rivets show past battles. Broken weapons (axe heads, spear tips, a chain-link wrap) are embedded in hide. Warm ember-orange glow on eyes, wounds and scars, and cold frost-blue glow on carved Nordic runes. Colour is only by place: darker scales on the back, lighter belly and underside, ash/mud at the feet, rust at the iron. Parts reach the same joints through shared mounts so seams hide inside overlapping volumes. Necks start buried inside the torso.

parts.builds: The barrel body: one loft over pelvis/spine1/chest (stations around z -1.9 r0.7, z -1 r1.0, z 0 r1.15, z 1.2 r1.2 hump, z 2.1 r0.9; centre y ~2.2, half-height ~1.0, half-width ~1.1), scaleDark on the back and scaleMid on the flanks via sectors, with a pale belly (belly / bellyDark) from the underside up the flanks. A big shoulder hump with five collar mounds (scaleMid, each ringed with small bone spikes) where each neck enters, at neckBaseC/IL/IR/OL/OR, so the necks emerge from inside the body. A dorsal ridge of broad overlapping bone plates and spikes (bone with boneDark bases) running from the hump to the rump, big at the shoulders and small at the hips. Rib bands and belly plates (bellyDark rows). Battle damage: three long pale scar gashes (scar) across the flanks, with a few ember-glowing seams, and two cauterised burn patches (ash and blood). Embedded broken weapons: an axe head (iron with a rust edge and a broken leather-wrapped shaft stump) stuck in the left flank, and a snapped spear tip in the right shoulder. A rusty chain (ironDark/rust torus links) loosely wrapped diagonally around the barrel with an iron buckle plate. Carved Nordic rune brand on each flank, 5 runes as small parts glowing frost, in a ring of ironDark. Stubby hip and shoulder muscle masses overlap the leg tops (the legs part owns the legs themselves). Glow kit on runes, wounds and scar seams.
parts.attaches: Necks start inside the collar mounds at neckBase* mounts (the head parts own the necks). Legs hang from shoulderL/R and hipL/R. The tail starts at tailRoot, which the torso rump covers with a rounded cap.

parts.builds: All four legs, owning their thigh and shoulder masses and feet. Forelegs are short, thick, pillar-like with a heavy shoulder blob (scaleMid) and a bone elbow spike each, sweeping smoothly from shoulderF* to elbowF*, wristF* and pawF* (radii 0.42 at the shoulder down to 0.22 at the wrist). Hindlegs are digitigrade: big thigh from hipH* to a forward knee, long shin back to a hock with a bone hock spur, then a lower leg forward to pawH*. Paws are chunky splayed three-toed feet, 3 toes each in scaleDark with ash dirt on the lower parts, and thick curved bone claws (claw colour, three per paw, forward). Every paw rests flat on y=0 (the feet sink at most 2%). Armoured wear: an iron cuff with a rust band and 4 rivets on one wrist, a bronze band on the left hock, and a frayed leather strap with a chain length on a foreleg. A pale scar gash on a thigh, a patch of belly-pale hide on the inner legs, and ash/mud coloured lower leg bands. Rune frost glow at each shoulder (one small rune each).
parts.attaches: Hangs from the torso at shoulderL/R and hipL/R mounts. The leg joints are children of chest and pelvis.

parts.builds: A long heavy tail on tail1..tail6 from tailRoot (0,2.1,-1.7) to tailTip (0,1.05,-5.0): one smooth sweep with radius from ~0.6 down to 0.07, scaleDark back with a pale belly strip. A row of bone dorsal spikes growing smaller toward the tip, with boneDark bases. A bone spade/blade tip made as an extrude, with a notch and a chipped edge. Wounds: a ring of ironDark with rust ring bands near the middle, a thick chain wound twice around it, a broken harpoon head embedded near the tail root (iron head, leather rope tail), and a long scar with ember glow. Frost rune ring (3 small runes, glowing) around the tail root where the pelvis meets it. Ash-coloured dirt on the underside.
parts.attaches: Starts at tailRoot, overlapping the torso rump, and uses the tail1..tail6 joints.

parts.builds: The alpha centre head and neck, the hero piece (head scale H = 1.25: the skull is ~1.3 m long and 0.9 m wide). The neck is one smooth sweep over neckC1..neckC4 to headC: radius 0.5 at the base down to 0.33 at the head, scaleDark back, with a pale belly/throat strip made of banded throat plates. A row of bone dorsal spikes up the back of the neck and a ruffle frill of bone blades behind the skull. The skull is a faceted wedge with brow ridges over big ember eyes (glowing emberHot ring, pupil slit in pupil, an inset dark socket), a long blunt snout with nostril pits, with an upper jaw on headC carrying two rows of teeth (bone, big fangs at the front, chipped), and a separate lower jaw on jawC (scaleMid) with lower teeth and a mouth interior (mouth and tongue). A crown of 6 massive swept-back horns (hornDark with bone tips and boneDark rings), the two biggest curving outward. One horn is broken and capped with an iron band and rust rivets. A big scar gash over the left eye (scar tissue, ember glow seam). Iron muzzle ring with a short chain. Frost rune carved on the forehead (glowing). Cheek plates with spikes.
parts.attaches: The neck root is buried in the chest collar at neckBaseC; the head joint is at headSocketC, with the jaw at jawC. The torso is the neighbour at the base.

parts.builds: The two inner heads and necks (left L = +X, right R = -X), mirrored in design, head scale H = 1.0 (skull ~1.05 m long) with slightly different features: neck sweeps over neckIL1..IL4 / neckIR1..IR4 to headIL / headIR with radius 0.42 down to 0.28, scaleDark back and a pale throat strip, bone dorsal neck spikes, and a bone frill. Each head matches the centre head's design language at smaller scale: a faceted skull, brow ridges, glowing ember eyes (emberHot ring, pupil slit), nostrils, an upper jaw on the head joint with two rows of teeth, and a separate lower jaw on jawIL/jawIR (with mouth and tongue). Differences: the left head has a pair of long straight horns and an iron-banded snout; the right head has a ram-like pair of curled horns (spiral) and a scarred cheek with a stitched leather patch. Each has a small frost rune on the brow, and one pale scar across the snout.
parts.attaches: Neck roots are buried in the torso collars at neckBaseIL and neckBaseIR. The head joints are at headSocketIL/IR with jaws at jawIL/jawIR. The necks cross the space between the centre head (x 0) and the outer heads (x ±3) without touching them.

parts.builds: The two outer heads and necks (L = +X, R = -X), the lowest heads, head scale H = 0.85 (skull ~0.9 m long), angled outward, with thinner necks (radius 0.38 down to 0.24) sweeping over neckOL1..OL4 / neckOR1..OR4 to headOL / headOR. Same design language: scaleDark back, pale throat strip, bone dorsal neck spikes, faceted skull, brow ridges, ember eyes, nostrils, upper jaw on the head joint with teeth and a separate lower jaw on jawOL/jawOR with mouth and tongue. These are the most battle-worn: the left head is blind in one eye (a pale scarred, closed eye with a long scar across it and no glow) and has a snapped horn stump wrapped in leather and rust-iron, and a spear tip buried in its jaw; the right head has a cauterised half-severed neck wound (ash, blood and ember glowing seam, a bone ring plate stitched to the neck), one short horn and a broken tooth line. Both have small frost runes on the cheek.
parts.attaches: Neck roots are buried in the torso collars at neckBaseOL and neckBaseOR. The head joints are at headSocketOL/OR with jaws at jawOL/jawOR. The necks run outward and slightly forward under the inner necks.

calls.reasoning:
I'm sketching out a God of War-style five-headed hydra concept, weathered and Norse in feel with bronze/iron scars and runes, starting with the skeleton structure—torso, pelvis, four legs, claws, belly, and spine plates—before working out how to split the five heads and necks into logical groups.

I'm deciding to organize the heads into a center head, inner pair, and outer pair, plus a tail and back ridge section, so the whole creature breaks into six manageable parts. Since joints form the skeleton before any part is built, I need to carefully predefine the neck and jaw joint chains so each head-building part can sweep its geometry along those existing paths.

Now I'm roughing out overall scale and pose: a large quadruped body around six units wide and eight long, with the shoulder mound at the front spawning five fanned necks that arch upward and forward, each head angled outward at increasing distance from center, legs planted with feet near the ground, and the torso lofted between the rear and front of the body at a consistent height.

I'm beginning the joint hierarchy, starting with the pelvis, spine segments, and chest as the root parents, then preparing to branch out the individual neck chains from the chest joint.

For the center neck/head chain, I'm plotting joint positions rising from the chest in an S-curve, through neckC1-C4 up toward the head and jaw, leveling off slightly downward at the head so it reads as a naturally extended neck posture.

Now I'm working out the overall bounding box size, then mirroring the setup for the inner left/right necks offset from center, plotting their own joint coordinates curving outward and upward.

Settling on overall size [6.8, 5.6, 8.9] with varied head heights across the antler branches, angling the outer heads outward. Now I'm plotting the front leg joints—shoulder, elbow, wrist, and paw—positioning the shoulder and elbow coordinates for the front limb.

Now working out the hind leg joints too, placing hip, knee, hock, and paw positions with a digitigrade stance so the hock sits higher and back while the paw sits forward near the ground.

I'm plotting the tail chain as six segments curving gently down from the pelvis to a low sweeping tip, keeping it just above floor level, then assigning role labels like neck, head, jaw, leg, and tail to each joint group for parenting.

Now I'm defining the mount points and part hierarchy: torso owns the body loft, belly plates, spine ridge plates, and the collar mounds where necks emerge. For the Hydra's God of War aesthetic I'm going with a dark slate-green scaled hide, ash-grey belly, bone-white ridge spikes, and blood-red ember glow in the runes and eyes.

Torso also carries rune brands and embedded broken spear/axe heads as relic scars, with joints at pelvis, spine1, and chest. Legs are a separate part with four limbs, paws, claws, and bronze/iron armor bands, carrying the hip and shoulder mass, with the torso's bounding box allowed to overlap slightly. I'm moving on to defining the tail part next.

Giving the five heads variety—missing eye, severed stump, cauterized scar—to make the pack feel battle-worn. I'm defining a shared head spec for consistency across builders: skull wedge shape, hinged jaw with teeth, swept horns, ember-glowing eyes, dorsal spikes, with scaled proportions so the center head is largest (1.25), inner heads mid-sized (1.0), and outer heads smaller (0.85), along with matching neck taper radii for each.

I'm also working out a limited color palette under 24 swatches: dark green-grey scales for the back, pale cream-tan for the belly, bone tones for horns and teeth, and ember-orange glows, plus iron, rust, and bronze accents for any armor or weapon elements.

Now I'm budgeting the shape count across body parts—torso, legs, tail, two heads, and a center head—keeping the total under 900 while splitting it fairly between the segments.

I'm also thinking through the overall God of War aesthetic: gritty, Nordic, battle-worn, desaturated tones with ember/frost accents, chunky forms, scars, embedded broken weapons, glowing runes, and chains. Then I'm working out the joint hierarchy for the heads—skull built from the head joint, jaw as a separate piece hinged below and forward, with neck spikes following the bone curve via catmull interpolation.

Now I'm refining the actual coordinates for the neck-to-head chain, plotting control points so the neck curves upward then forward into the head joint position, adjusting directions at each segment so the final sweep feels natural rather than stiff.

Continuing outer outline points to the head, giving width 7.2. Now I'm sketching rough neck bone directions pointing toward successive joints, and starting to lay out bounding boxes for the head geometry.

I'm working out the body loft stations along the spine, with radius tapering from tail root to chest, and placing the pelvis joint and neck bases so the neck bases sit embedded inside the torso's shoulder collar.

Now I'm laying out the joint hierarchy: pelvis as root, spine1 and chest extending forward, and a chain of tail joints extending backward with decreasing y and radius down to the tail tip.

For the limbs, I'm defining front legs parented to chest and hind legs parented to pelvis, placing shoulder, elbow, wrist, and paw joints with directional offsets for the left side, then planning to mirror these positions onto the right side using negative x values.

Now I'm working out the hind leg joint chain—hip, knee, hock, and paw—with their positions and direction vectors so the leg bends naturally toward the toes.

Then I'm tallying the total joint count across spine, tail, legs, neck, head, and jaw to confirm it hits 55, and starting to lay out head and jaw coordinates for the center, inner, and outer figures with their downward-forward tilt.

Now I'm mirroring these for the right side, then moving to list out all mounts and begin writing the full JSON with detailed builds, keeping descriptions concise, grounding the legs on the floor with a slight sink for the hind paw.
